solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Primate's over-familiar addressing of the President?

blocks.note: first meaning: a small nocturnal African primate with big eyes
second meaning: calling President George W. Bush by a pet name

explanation.surface: A cheeky aide sidles up to the leader of the free world and calls him a pet name.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2008 the President was George W. Bush; tacking on 'baby' is the over-familiar address. The 's after Primate is just the join.
explanation.definitionFit: The galago of African forests is commonly called by this name, a small tree-dwelling primate.

clue.text: Writer loosened bra (it could help you achieve a rise)

definitions.text: it could help you achieve a rise

indicators.note: something loosened has come undone and its parts shift, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky aside about a loosened bra, with the hint that it might arouse someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The rise is a baking one: bicarbonate of soda is a raising agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicarbonate of soda releases carbon dioxide when heated, making cakes and bread puff up in the oven.

clue.text: Unpleasant, being the source of an obnoxious leak

definitions.text: the source of an obnoxious leak

blocks.note: first meaning: rude, haughty, nasty in manner

blocks.clueFragment: the source of an obnoxious leak
blocks.note: second meaning: describing a runny nose dripping mucus

explanation.surface: A disagreeable person is accused of being behind a nasty press leak.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'leak' sounds like a political leak to the papers, but it is from a runny nose.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both supercilious and unpleasant in manner, and literally running with nasal mucus.

clue.text: Dicky Yates (Lab) ropes Right in for back-stabbings

indicators.note: to rope in someone is to draw them inside a group, so a letter joins the rest
completes the phrasal verb, saying the extra letter goes inside the others
dicky is British slang for faulty or shaky, so the letters are out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A Labour man called Dicky Yates recruits someone from the right wing, a treacherous move.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a first name but means unsound; R is added to the letters before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Back-stabbing is figurative treachery against an ally, which is what acts of disloyalty or treason are.

clue.text: (+ 25dn.) Vomit put one off regular boozer

indicators.note: putting something off here means taking it away, so one letter is dropped

blocks.note: barf is slang for vomit
to lay something is to put it down
a means one; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker's being sick has put someone off going to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' is British for a pub as well as a drinker; here it is the drinker who is a regular.
explanation.definitionFit: A barfly is someone who spends a lot of time drinking in bars, a habitual drinker.

clue.text: He's fit (unusual for a sex object)

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal order, so the letters before it get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a man is attractive, then adds that this is an unusual object of lust.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetish is an object or body part on which sexual desire becomes fixated, so a sex object in the literal sense.

clue.text: Forced evacuation east, the last word in retreat

indicators.note: a retreating army goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for east
amen is the final word of a prayer

explanation.surface: A military report of troops being made to pull out of the east, with a final word on the retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema injects fluid into the bowel to make it empty, a bowel movement brought about artificially.

clue.text: Tory in, eh? (Corrupt, it can be assumed)

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or distorted, so the letters before it are twisted out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Conservative gets into power, and the cynic shrugs that he is surely on the take.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something holds in theory means it is supposed or presumed to be so, without proof in practice.

clue.text: Den Skinner's thing (openly gay)

blocks.note: a skinner works with animal skins, or hides
someone out has openly declared being gay

explanation.surface: Reads as Labour MP Dennis Skinner, nicknamed the Beast of Bolsover, having a secret about being openly gay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Den Skinner' looks like the MP Dennis Skinner, but Den is the definition and a skinner is a tradesman.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is a secret lair or bolt-hole where someone hides away, which is a hideout.

clue.text: Monarch taking piss over Paddy exercising

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word for urine is read backwards
taking something in means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a king is a monarch
pee is slang for urine
a paddy is a fit of temper

explanation.surface: A king mocks an Irishman who is working out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking the piss' is British slang for mocking; 'paddy' looks like a slang term for an Irishman, but in British usage a paddy is also a temper tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping fit means staying in good physical shape through regular workouts, which is what exercising is.

clue.text: see 16dn.
Brown would like to be let off with decree

definitions.note: the definition completes a sentence: Brown would like to be re-elected

indicators.note: a thing gone off has spoiled and is no longer in its proper state, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Prime Minister Gordon Brown hopes to escape trouble by issuing an official order.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a sentence fragment: Gordon Brown, Prime Minister in 2008, would like to be returned to office at the next election.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician facing a vote wants to win another term, which is exactly being voted back into office.

clue.text: English place to engage in beastly sex? Get off!

blocks.note: to rut is to mate, as stags do in season
to land is to get off a plane or boat, to alight

explanation.surface: A smutty question about a place for animal mating, answered by an indignant 'Get off!'
explanation.walkthrough: Rutland is England's smallest historic county, in the East Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Rutland is a county in England, so it is an English place in the geographical sense.

clue.text: Chow that's gobbled by chow?

blocks.note: surface reading: food eaten greedily by someone
setter's reading: the second chow is a chow chow, a breed of dog, so this is food for a dog

explanation.walkthrough: Chow means food, and a chow is also a fluffy Chinese dog breed, so the clue describes canine food.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard baked snack made for pets is fed to dogs, a breed like the chow being an obvious eater.

clue.text: Pretend medicine is to fix stinking problem

blocks.note: to place something is to fix or set it in position
BO stands for body odour

explanation.surface: A doctor claims a sham remedy can cure a smelly complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is an inert pill given as if it were a real drug, so it is medicine only in pretence.

clue.text: Supporting computers, etc. like a comic desperate for a one-night stand?

blocks.note: a comic is busy making gags, so gagging
to be for something is to support it
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A comedian who backs the tech crowd is apparently eager for a casual fling.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces read in a different order from the clue: the comic's part comes first, then supporting, then computers.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase means sexually eager, someone who would welcome a quick casual encounter.

clue.text: (& 10ac.) Economic power? Sarkozy's end calculation scuppered

indicators.note: a scuppered plan is wrecked, so the letters of the word before it are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: fin is French for end, and Sarkozy was the French President
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nicolas Sarkozy's economic plan comes undone in a miscalculation.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarkozy's end is not his last letter Y but the French word for end, since he was French President.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout means influence or power, so the financial kind is economic power wielded through money.

clue.text: Horseshit collection from Brown: The Man Entering the Breach

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
he is the pronoun for a man
a gap is a breach or opening

explanation.surface: Mocks Gordon Brown as the man stepping into the breach, with the verdict that it is all nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown is again Gordon Brown on the surface, but here it is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A dung-heap is a pile of manure, so a heap of horse droppings literally.

clue.text: Addictive behaviour that gets up the nose?

definitions.text: Addictive behaviour that gets up the nose?

blocks.clueFragment: Addictive behaviour that gets up the nose?
blocks.note: surface reading: a habit that irritates people, since 'gets up your nose' means annoys
setter's reading: a habit where a solvent is literally inhaled through the nose

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets up your nose' is a British idiom for annoying someone; here it is meant literally, of fumes being breathed in.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhaling adhesive solvent vapour for a high is a well-known form of substance abuse that can become a habit.

clue.text: Force knocks up bitches

blocks.note: g is the symbol for gravitational force
to knock someone up, in British usage, is to wake them by knocking

explanation.surface: A crude claim that someone forcibly impregnates female dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocks up' sounds like impregnates, but in British English it also means wakes someone by knocking on the door; bitches is the verb meaning complains.
explanation.definitionFit: To bitch is to complain moaningly, and to grouse is likewise to grumble, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Renounce the Spencer family?

blocks.note: Di's, belonging to Diana Spencer, Princess of Wales
one's own means one's family or kin

explanation.surface: Asks whether one should cut ties with Princess Diana's aristocratic family.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spencer here is Diana, born Lady Diana Spencer, so the family is Di's own.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown is to refuse to acknowledge as one's own, which is to renounce or repudiate.

clue.text: Fervent plea from Rex, hugged by settler

indicators.note: being hugged means being held inside someone's arms, so this letter goes within the next word

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king
one who settles a bill is the payer

explanation.surface: A heartfelt appeal comes from a king embraced by a colonist.
explanation.walkthrough: A settler looks like a colonist but is one who settles a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer is an earnest request, whether to God or to a person, so a heartfelt entreaty.

clue.text: Penis possibly extended by capless biro – it's grown, naturally

indicators.note: something extended has more added on its end, so the next piece follows on
without a cap means the top, here the first letter, is taken away

blocks.note: the penis is an example of a bodily organ, hence 'possibly'
Bic is a famous brand of ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: A crude boast about an enlargement aided by a pen, insisting the growth is all natural.
explanation.walkthrough: A biro is a ballpoint pen, so a Bic; losing its cap drops the B.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is farmed without synthetic chemicals, so it is grown by natural methods.

clue.text: Old-fashioned twit takes wife for Labour's leader (only just)

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the first letter of the word before is used
taking one thing for another means swapping it in, so one letter is replaced

blocks.note: nelly is a dated British term for a silly person
W is the abbreviation for wife
the opening letter of Labour

explanation.surface: A fusty old fool marries and so becomes, barely, the head of the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: The W replaces the first L of the old word for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Newly means recently, and something only just done has happened a moment ago.

clue.text: African place forms line, pressing to shag boyfriend's head off

indicators.note: a head is the front, so only the opening letter of that word is meant
taking something off means removing it, here from the word for sex
pressing something to oneself means holding it close inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a tier is a row or line, as of seats
slang for having sex
the opening letter of boyfriend

explanation.surface: An African town where people queue up, eager to bed a man while losing their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: The B is removed from the slang word for sex, and what remains sits inside the word for a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangier is a port city in northern Morocco on the Strait of Gibraltar, so a place in Africa.

clue.text: Second west London area to cause a stink (crooked)

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
Kew, home of the botanic gardens, is in west London
to whiff is to smell bad

explanation.surface: Someone in a west London suburb makes a fuss, and the whole thing seems a bit dodgy.
explanation.definitionFit: Skew-whiff is British informal for askew, out of line or not straight, so tilted and crooked.

clue.text: see 4dn.
Mockery of press at Tory's end

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: to iron clothes is to press them
the final letter of Tory

explanation.surface: The newspapers jeer at a Conservative politician whose career has hit the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' acts as a positional join here: the Y sits at the end, after the press word.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony is a mode of speech that says the opposite of what is meant, often to deride or ridicule.

clue.text: Yes-s, drunken guards pisspot imperial soldiers

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about unsteadily, so the letters before it are jumbled
to guard something is to surround and protect it, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: a slurred 'yes' with a hiss on the end, taken as letters
a po is a chamber pot

explanation.surface: A drunk slurs agreement while soldiers of the empire keep watch over a chamber pot.
explanation.walkthrough: A po is a British word for a chamber pot, a bedroom potty.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepoys were Indian infantrymen serving under British command in the Raj, soldiers of the empire.

clue.text: Organ Craft puts emphasis on viewers

definitions.note: a verb phrase describing what the noun does

blocks.note: the eye is an organ of the body
an ocean liner is a seagoing craft

explanation.surface: Reads like a headline about a music-making firm playing up to a TV audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viewers' are eyes, so the definition describes make-up that outlines and highlights them.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeliner is cosmetic drawn around the lids to make the eyes stand out and look more striking.
